newsitem.title: GREECE: Athens bourse fails to open, settlement row rages.
newsitem.headline: Athens bourse fails to open, settlement row rages.

text.p: The Athens bourse failed to open for the second working day, with brokers in an uproar over how to deal with a settlement crisis after one firm defaulted with the exchange's clearing house last week.
Bourse president Manolis Xanthakis joined a stormy meeting on Monday of all 65 brokerages at the Association of Athens Stock Exchange Members (SMEXA) to try to resolve the crisis.
"The prevailing sentiment is that we won't open, the odds are against this happening. As it stands, there are 65 different opinions on how to tackle the problem," said one broker.

The crisis broke last week when Delta Securities defaulted on 2.6 billion drachmas owed to the exchange's clearing house. The clearing house, in turn, withheld cash settlement payments to a number of brokerages, prompting the uproar.
A number of brokerages said they had no confidence they would be paid by the clearing house unless the bourse acted quickly to sort out the mess.

Fraud charges were then brought against Delta Securities and its senior officials told not to leave Greece. Bourse sources said Delta's default appeared linked to trades involving Magrizos, a textile firm.
Magrizos shares were trading at 201 drachmas on September 1, 1995, and soared to a 1,365-drachma high on September 13, 1996, before starting to plummet. They closed at 911 on November 7.
Many brokers said about a half dozen firms were involved in the Magrizos trades that eventually brought down Delta.
"If the picture is not sorted out and authorities do not disclose which members were on the sell side for shares of Magrizos the bourse should not open," one broker said.
Only Delta has been charged with wrongdoing and the SMEXA members seem to be divided over whether there should be a full-blown investigation or they should get back to business as usual quickly.

"We should get auditors to move in and carry out audits on every member firm. The exchange should stay closed until everything that went wrong is brought to light," said Vassilis Hatzelias, managing director of Intersec, one of Athens large brokerages.

Bourse officials announced on Friday they were freezing the bank accounts and assets of Delta Securities, and sealing its offices and safe, after Delta was found to be in the red with the bourse clearing house for 2.6 billion drachmas.
